Yes, definitely yes: my twins do nót have the same character. I could feel that in the womb even. And that translates directly to how they sleep and how the get there. A needs comfort, B needs to do his own thing. A needed to cry to process his day before falling asleep. He still sucks his thumb at 2 years old, which serves the same purpose. B winds down by playing in the dark. Even as a baby, he would play by kicking his sheets, by rolling around. He needed space to do so, so we transferred him to a bigger bed to be able to do so. Both of them need their own space and time to wind down. So we let them. I did not hold A longer so he won't cry: because he needed that cry to sleep, me holding him was only prolonging his bedtime, he was going to cry anyway, as he needed it. And I would definitely not try to sooth B or put him down again and again. He needed to play and do his own thing to wind down. He has never fallen asleep because we tried to get him to. He prefers his own space. It took us a while to get there, to understand that we were only getting in their way by trying to help them to sleep. Be it for their own reasons. But if your baby, with a completely different character than my boys, needs you to hold them: you hold them. If your baby needs to be rocked: rock them. If they need you to wait in the room while they do their thing: wait. You are not failing as a parent because your baby has more difficulties to fall asleep. Your child just might need a whole lot more help to get there. Which is tough and feels unfair, and it might tire you out. But if that is what your baby needs, that's what they should get.
